chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similar to it.
Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ubaydullah al-Dahqan, from Durust, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)
He said: 'From what Adam (peace be upon him) bequeathed to his son Hibatullah was: "Eat the olives, for they are from a blessed tree."'
ai.seo_question: What did Adam (peace be upon him) advise his son regarding olives?
ai.summary: This narration, transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni in *Al-Kafi*, links the physical virtue of olives to their primordial origin, attributing the advice to Adam (peace be upon him) as a timeless prescription for health. In Shia scholarly tradition, this underscores the concept of *al-Tab'* (natural disposition), where the olive is viewed not merely as food but as a blessed entity (*shajarah mubarakah*) connecting human physiology to divine wisdom. The emphasis on consumption reflects the broader Islamic emphasis on preventive medicine and the spiritual purity associated with simple, blessed foods.
